title: Noise stability and the noise operator
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $ho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Choose $X$ uniformly from the sign cube and, independently in each coordinate, obtain $Y$ by keeping $X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and otherwise flipping its sign. If $T_\rho$ is the linear operator that multiplies each Walsh monomial of degree $k$ by $\rho^k$, then $\mathbb E[f(X)f(Y)]=\langle f,T_\rho f\rangle$, where the inner product is the uniform average over the sign cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
